title: Polymer Brush-Mediated Surface-Initiated Polycondensation Enables sp2C-COF Thin Films with Controlled Crystallinity and High Photocatalytic Performance
abstract: Sp2-carbon-conjugated covalent organic frameworks (sp2C-COFs) hold exceptional potential as π-conjugated semiconductors for optoelectronics and photocatalysis, yet their thin-film fabrication suffers from irreversible C = C linkages that impede crystallinity and morphology control. Herein, we report a polymer brush-mediated surface-initiated polycondensation (PB-SIP) strategy to synthesize the sp2C-COF films with controlled crystallinity and morphology. The polymer brush layer acts as both a surface-tethered initiator and a soft interfacial regulator, enabling precise control over nucleation and crystallization kinetics. By modulating the polymer brush thickness, we achieve sp2C-COF films with enhanced crystallinity and reduced surface roughness. Notably, this method allows the growth of highly crystalline, homogeneous sp2C-COF coatings on 3D porous sponges, which exhibit near-complete photocatalytic antibacterial efficiency (99.4%) in natural sewage under visible light. This interfacial engineering paradigm advances the rational design of crystalline sp2C-COF films for energy-environment applications. Conjugated covalent organic frameworks (COF) hold exceptional potential as semiconductors for optoelectronics and photocatalysis, but control over crystallinity and morphology remains challenging. Here the authors report a polymer brush- mediated surface-initiated polycondensation strategy to synthesize the conjugated COF films with controlled crystallinity and morphology.

title: Stable Open-Shell Bowl-Shaped Cycloarene with Multiple Hybrid Spin–Spin Coupling and Tunable Radical Characters
abstract: Abstract The precise syntheses of well-defined cycloarenes and stable open-shell polyradicaloids are two challenging topics in chemistry and materials science. Herein, the first example of a cycloarene polyradicaloid molecule (CPR) with three types of adjacent spin–spin coupling was successfully synthesized in single-crystal form by fusing Chichibabin, Schlenk, and o-quinodimethane hydrocarbons into a conjugated double-stranded bowl structure. It exhibits a small singlet–triplet energy gap, significant polyradical characters, and remarkable stability (t1/2 = 110 days in air-saturated solution). Interestingly, CPR adapts a rigid oval-bowl-shaped configuration and demonstrates fascinating encapsulation of fullerenes C60 and C70. Crucially, various experimental results confirm that the intramolecular spin–spin interactions can be effectively modulated by an electron-accepting guest, which represents the first systematic study of the radical characters in π-conjugated polyradicaloids by a supramolecular assembly strategy. Our findings provide a new approach for constructing stable cycloarene polyradicaloids and a novel strategy for manipulating radical spin coupling.

title: Framework Excavation of UiO‐66 for In Situ Confined Cu 3 Cluster Assembly Toward Nitrite Electroreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Heterogenizing molecular catalysts requires the simultaneous preservation of structural precision, active‐site accessibility, and long‐term stability. To address the limited capacity of robust small‐pore frameworks for molecular clusters and the susceptibility of large‐pore hosts to guest leaching and structural degradation, we propose a “Framework Excavation” strategy. This strategy selectively creates local enlargements within the microporous framework to generate sufficient space for the in situ formation of metal clusters, while the retained narrow channels kinetically confine the as‐formed clusters and allow substrates to pass through the pores to fully access the highly exposed cluster sites. As a demonstration, chemically stable UiO‐66 was engineered with missing‐Zr 6 ‐node defects and employed as a host for the ship‐in‐a‐bottle assembly of Cu 3 molecular clusters, yielding Cu 3 @UiO‐66‐Exc. In electrocatalytic nitrite reduction, Cu 3 @UiO‐66‐Exc achieves an NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 98.7% and a yield rate of 19.21 mg cm −2 h −1 , with stable performance over 300 h of cumulative electrolysis. Mechanistic studies, including DMPO‐H spin‐trapping, in situ infrared spectroscopy and theoretical computations, reveal that the confined Cu 3 architecture promotes active‐hydrogen generation and successive hydrogenation of nitrogen‐containing intermediates. This work establishes a catalyst support design principle that enables the in situ generation, long‐term retention, and high site accessibility of molecular clusters within a robust microporous framework.

title: Development of Ester-Based Covalent Organic Framework Film Optical Waveguides for Their Competitive SO2 Gas Sensing Application
abstract: Abstract Ester-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs) demonstrate improved sensing stability and enhanced dipole–dipole (μ–μ) interactions for competitive SO2 sensing upon various acidic gases. An ester-based COF, referred to as [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF, was synthesized using biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarboxylic acid (H4bptc) monomer and 4,4′,4″-(1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triyl) triphenol (TOPT) linker through a one-pot solvothermal method. The resulting COF films were optically transparent and exhibited an irregular hexagonal mesoporous architecture and a high refractive index (from 1.7247 to1.9073), which supports strong single-mode (TE0) guided light, meeting the essential criteria for an optical waveguide sensor (OWGS). As an OWGS, the [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF film demonstrated high efficiency in SO2 sensing upon various acidic gases. The spectral analysis and density-functional theory computations indicated that the ester group and benzene ring in [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF contribute to SO2 sensing through μ–μ interactions, which are associated with increased adsorption energy, elongated ester bond length, and reduced bond angles, leading to an increase in the refractive index, adsorption coefficient, and almost reversible morphological change of the [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF. The presented OWGS features a fast response (tres = 2 s), a wide detection range (100 ppm to 10 ppb), a low detection limit (2.5 ppb), and excellent resistance to interference at 293 K despite its weak immunity to humidity. Furthermore, SO2 adsorption weight of 17.18 ng·cm–2 was determined on per unit area of the [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF film surface upon μ–μ interactions.

title: Covalently Locked Donor–Acceptor Block Copolymer Nanoparticles Enable Efficient, Stable and Reproducible Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic photocatalysts with tailored properties and unique processability offer a sustainable route to solar hydrogen. To maximize light harvesting and charge generation, donor and acceptor materials are usually physically mixed to form D:A heterojunction nanoparticles (NPs). However, weakly constrained interactions can promote phase segregation, morphological evolution, and limited reproducibility. Here, we introduce an all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymer, PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT, in which covalent linkage between PBDB‐T and PYT segments constrains nanoscale donor–acceptor organization and promotes intramolecular charge transfer. Compared with nanoparticles prepared from a physical PBDB‐T:PYT blend, PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT nanoparticles exhibit stronger photoluminescence quenching, more persistent charge‐associated transient absorption features, and improved photoelectrochemical charge extraction. As a result, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) rates exceeding 120 mmol cm −2 g −1 h −1 (>450 µmol h −1 ) are achieved with low Pt loading (<3 wt.%). PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT NPs retained 95% of the initial HER rate after 96 h of photocatalysis. Conversely, NPs prepared from physically mixed PBDB‐T and PYT show lower activity and faster deactivation, consistent with morphology‐driven losses. PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT also maintains high performance across polymer batches, improving reproducibility. These results establish all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymers as a promising design strategy for combining high activity, operational stability, and reproducibility in organic nanoparticle photocatalysis.

title: Promoting C–S Coupling for Hydroxymethanesulfonate Electrosynthesis over Cu-Mn Phthalocyanine Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic C–S coupling to synthesize high-value organosulfur chemicals represents a sustainable paradigm shift from traditional thermochemical processes, yet the electrocatalytic performance remains far from satisfactory. Herein, we develop Cu-Mn bimetallic phthalocyanine metal–organic frameworks (PcCu-Mn) as a highly efficient catalyst for hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) synthesis from CO2 and SO32–. When operated in a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer, PcCu-Mn delivers a record-high HMS yield rate of 285.4 mmol h–1 g–1 and a high Faradaic efficiency of 51.2% along with long-term stability for over 200 h of electrolysis. Mechanistic operando spectroscopic and theoretical investigations reveal the spatial synergy of Cu-Mn dual sites to enable the simultaneous CO2 reduction into electrophilic *CHOH and SO32– activation into nucleophilic *SO3 while promoting *CHOH/*SO3 intermolecular C–S bond formation for selective HMS generation. Furthermore, a comprehensive techno-economic analysis validates the commercial viability of HMS production via the PcCu-Mn-driven electrochemical C–S coupling route.

title: Accelerated Zeolite Defect Healing Suppresses Oxygen-Containing Species Trapping for Tandem Propene Epoxidation
abstract: Abstract Selective oxidation of chemical feedstocks with in situ-generated H2O2 offers a sustainable route to high-value oxygenates, yet such tandem catalysis is often fundamentally limited by the trapping of oxygen-containing species, including H2O2-derived intermediates and oxygenated products in zeolite microenvironments, where they undergo nonproductive decomposition and side reactions. Herein, we overcome this limitation by accelerating titanosilicalite hydroxyl defect healing through intensified nucleation and subsequent accelerated crystal growth. The resulting defect-healed microenvironment facilitates the transport of in situ-generated H2O2 between bifunctional active sites while suppressing its nonproductive decomposition to H2O. Moreover, it accelerates product propylene oxide (PO) desorption by weakening hydrogen bond interactions between PO and hydroxyl defects, thereby suppressing ring-opening and overoxidation side reactions. Consequently, the defect-healed Au/TS-1 catalyst exhibits a 1.8-fold enhancement in the PO formation rate and a 2.1-fold increase in Au-based productivity. This defect-healing strategy is broadly applicable to titanosilicates, aluminosilicates, and pure-silica zeolites and can be readily extended to a 10 L scale process, delivering reductions of 21% in production cost and 54% in carbon emissions compared with conventional TS-1 synthesis. Overall, this work establishes a sustainable, scalable, and cost-effective route for zeolite defect healing and provides a general strategy to overcome the long-standing transport-decomposition trade-off in tandem catalysis with in situ-generated H2O2.

title: Dynamic Supramolecular Probe With Chloride‐Guided Assembly and DNA‐Mediated Intracellular Reorganization for Tumor Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Subcellularly targeted molecules usually act through static localization, whereas systems that undergo environment‐triggered state transitions and functional reprogramming remain underexplored. Here, we develop alkyl‐chain‐tunable Ly‐Cn molecules whose intracellular behavior is governed by chloride‐dependent assembly and DNA‐mediated supramolecular reorganization. Responsiveness varies nonmonotonically with chain length, with Ly‐12 achieving an optimal balance. At physiologically relevant chloride concentrations, Ly‐12 undergoes a threshold‐like aggregation transition into supramolecular nanoparticles that are subsequently reorganized and disassembled by DNA. This dual‐responsive process drives initial accumulation in lysosome‐associated compartments, followed by lysosome‐to‐nucleus redistribution and DNA‐mediated nuclear trapping. Ly‐12 thereby acts beyond passive nuclear targeting: it initiates lysosomal perturbation that propagates into oxidative stress, endoplasmic‐reticulum stress, and DNA damage, while white‐light irradiation amplifies this cascade. Transcriptomic analysis corroborates the progressive stress response. In HeLa xenografts, intratumoral Ly‐12 produces marked antitumor efficacy that is further enhanced by white‐light irradiation, without evident systemic toxicity. These findings establish an environment‐responsive supramolecular strategy that converts ion‐regulated assembly and organelle redistribution into light‐amplified therapeutic activity.

title: Dual-Functional Structure-Directing Agents Enable High-Loading Encapsulation of Ultrasmall Metal Nanoparticles in Zeolites
abstract: Abstract Confined ultrasmall metal nanoparticles within zeolite crystals have emerged as promising catalysts due to their exceptional thermal stability and high catalytic activity under harsh reaction conditions. However, their loading amounts are limited to 1.0 mol % relative to SiO2, mainly due to steric hindrance and competition between metal species and structure-directing agents (SDAs) for access to micropores. Here, we introduce a molecular design strategy that unifies metal coordination and zeolite templating within a single dual-functional SDA molecule. This approach enables elevated metal loadings (up to ∼2.4 mol % relative to SiO2) of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. This strategy is applicable to multiple microporous frameworks, including MFI zeolites and AFI aluminophosphate, allowing encapsulation of Cu, Co, and Pt nanoparticles. The metal encapsulation by microporous crystals renders them stable under harsh reaction conditions (e.g., high temperature) and thereby suppresses catalyst deactivation through sintering during the methane dry reforming reaction. We believe that our approach offers a molecular design principle for the synthesis of high-loading, sintering-resistant, zeolite-encapsulated catalysts.

title: Chirality-Directed Molecular Weaving
abstract: Abstract Weaving molecular strands in a manner akin to macroscale fabrics is considered a highly promising strategy for the development of novel polymeric materials. However, existing molecular weaving strategies rely on metal templates or solvent assistance for topological control, which limits molecular weaving to specific conditions. Here, we present a new molecular weaving strategy based on chirality-directed assembly. It can be used in the construction of two-dimensional molecularly woven polymers in various solvents and at different temperatures, all without the use of metal templates or solvent assistance. Furthermore, leveraging the characteristic undulating structure of the woven topology, this strategy provides a unique pathway for tuning the porous separation performance and mechanical properties of molecularly woven materials. These advancements will expedite molecular weaving technology with unprecedented properties.

title: Topology-Engineered Dual-Functional COFs with Spatially Cooperated Hydrophilic and Photocatalytic Sites for Harvesting Safe Water from Polluted Atmosphere
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) has emerged as a promising decentralized solution for freshwater supply in off-grid regions by extracting ubiquitous moisture from the air. However, the atmosphere also carries airborne pathogens and, under extreme scenarios, toxic chemicals, which can be coharvested to contaminate the collected water. Despite extensive efforts to maximize water uptake, the safety of the harvested water has been largely neglected in the pursuit of higher water production yields. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide crystalline, molecularly programmable platforms for integrating water adsorption with photocatalytic detoxification. However, achieving such functional synergy depends on framework topology, which governs site accessibility and mass transport. Here, we report topology-engineered dual-functional COFs that regulate spatial cooperation among hydrophilic sites, photoactive sites, and pore structures in a series of 1D and 2D hydrazone COFs constructed from identical molecular building blocks. Compared to the compact 1D chain packing, the open and continuous channels of the 2D framework increase functional-site accessibility, support hydrogen-bonded water network formation, and facilitate charge-carrier separation and O2 activation. The optimized Por-TAH (2D) exhibits a saturated water uptake of 629 mg g–1, releases 94% of adsorbed water under mild heating, inactivates 99.99% of S. aureus within 1 h, and completely converts chemical agents with high selectivity within 10 min. As a proof-of-concept application, continuous-flow operation demonstrates integrated water harvesting and photocatalytic detoxification, yielding safe water free of detectable mustard gas simulants. This study establishes topology-directed spatial cooperation as a design principle for multifunctional porous materials, enabling safe water production from real contaminated air.

title: Surface-Layer Pore Aperture Engineering in a Metal–Organic Framework for High-Capacity CO2/C2H2 Molecular Sieving
abstract: Abstract Molecular sieving in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is commonly achieved by narrowing the entire pore network, which enhances size exclusion but often sacrifices adsorption capacity. Here we report surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a spatially decoupled strategy for high-capacity CO2/C2H2 molecular sieving. Through surface-confined coordination modification of a copper-based MOF, the external pore apertures were selectively regulated while the internal adsorption space was largely preserved. Microscopy, elemental mapping, depth-resolved XPS, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support the formation of a surface-confined functional shell at the pore aperture. The modified framework converts a nonselective, high-capacity adsorbent into a CO2/C2H2 molecular sieve. BUT-169-NH2-TRZ retains a high CO2 uptake of 90.3 cm3 g–1 at 298 K and 1 bar while suppressing C2H2 adsorption to 2.7 cm3 g–1, representing a new benchmark for CO2/C2H2 sieving separation. Further optimization with hexylamine affords faster CO2 transport and dynamic CO2/C2H2 separation, delivering a high productivity of 1.13 mol kg–1 for C2H2 (purity &gt; 99.99%) over repeated breakthrough cycles. This work establishes surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a route to overcome the conventional selectivity–capacity trade-off in molecular sieving separations.

title: Disentangling Modulator and Fluoride Chemistry in Rare-Earth Metal–Organic Framework Formation via Multinuclear NMR Spectroscopy: A Mechanism-Guided Synthetic Redesign
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF) chemistry continues to expand, highlighting the need for molecular insight into framework formation. Solution-phase NMR provides a powerful, accessible, and economical means to probe these mechanisms. We examine the formation of rare-earth (RE) UiO-66, focusing on Yttrium(III)-UiO-66. RE-UiO-66 contains a hexa-metallic node in which the metals are bridged by μ3-fluorido, μ3-hydroxido, and/or μ3-oxido ligands, with benzenedicarboxylate linkers connecting nodes. The fluorido ligand derives from the α-fluorinated modulators required for this synthesis, yet its formation and incorporation pathways are unclear. Using in situ multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, we demonstrate that MOF formation proceeds via zero-order kinetics. Modulator is consumed approximately an order of magnitude faster than linker. The fluoride ligand is formed via nucleophilic aromatic substitution between modulator and in situ-generated dimethylamine. Mass balance suggests that the modulator plays a dual role, coordinating to the metal cation and generating fluoride. However, when solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the modulator acts primarily as a fluoride source; in situ-formed acetic acid acts as the modulator. Thus, the dual modulator role can be decoupled; benzoic acid functions as the modulator and tetramethylammonium fluoride serves as the fluoride source. Under these modified conditions, linker consumption is slow. When solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the reaction accelerates. This highlights the complex influence of acidity, competitive binding of fluoride, modulator, and linker on kinetically labile rare-earth metals. The tetramethylammonium fluoride procedure provides a versatile pathway to RE-UiO-66 derivatives (RE = Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Yb, Lu) and two Y-UiO-67 derivatives.

title: Dynamic Soft‐Confinement via Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks Reshapes C–C Coupling Interfacial Chemistry at Bi 1 –Bi 2 Sites
abstract: ABSTRACT The core bottleneck in photocatalytic CO 2 reduction toward multi‐carbon oxygenates lies in the thermodynamic‐kinetic dual limitations of the C–C coupling step. Conventional strategies have focused on intrinsic electronic structure optimization of active sites while overlooking the critical influence of the reaction microenvironment on coupling probability. Herein, we propose a dynamic soft‐confinement catalytic strategy by in situ constructing a disordered hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF) layer on Bi 3 O 4 Br surfaces, thereby establishing an HOF/Bi 3 O 4 Br integrated photocatalytic system. The introduction of HOF not only induces the formation of asymmetric Bi 1 –Bi 2 coupling sites but also establishes a dynamic hydrogen‐bonding microenvironment surrounding them. This microenvironment enhances CO 2 coverage near the coupling sites by constructing a persistent carbon source enrichment layer. Simultaneously, the interfacial polarization field promotes exciton dissociation and directs electron transport toward the Bi 1 –Bi 2 sites. Furthermore, the reconfigurable hydrogen bonds impose orientational soft confinement on *CO intermediates, guiding them into spatial configurations favorable for *OCCO bond formation. This soft‐hard synergistic interfacial design enables 0.7HOF/Bi 3 O 4 Br to achieve a CH 3 COOH production rate of 325.12 µmol g −1 h −1 with 98.81% product selectivity under sacrificial agent‐free conditions. This work demonstrates that dynamic microenvironment programming around active sites constitutes a critical pathway for overcoming the photocatalytic C–C coupling bottleneck.

title: Quantum Confined One-Dimensional Lepidocrocite TiO2–Assisted In Situ Synthesis of ZIF-8 MOF: Hierarchical Porous Nanocomposites Exhibit Improved Li-ion Transport
abstract: Abstract One-dimensional (1D) nanostructured materials offer distinctive physical and chemical properties suitable for advanced energy applications. Among these, 1D lepidocrocite-type TiO2 (1DL), recently discovered, has shown potential in batteries, water splitting, wastewater treatment, and polymer composites, among others. In this study, we report on the combination of 1DL with an in situ formed metal–organic framework (MOF), specifically ZIF-8, to produce a hierarchically porous ZIF-8/1DL composite. X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirms the successful in situ formation of ZIF-8 in the presence of 1DL. In the composite, the average ZIF-8 size is ∼30 nm, that is smaller than that observed in conventional bulk syntheses that typically yield micron-scale crystals. Zeta-potential measurements indicate electrostatic interactions between positively charged ZIF-8 particles and negatively charged 1DL, which stabilize the composite. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping show a relatively uniform distribution of ZIF-8 on 1DL surfaces. Nitrogen adsorption–desorption analyses reveal a substantial increase in specific surface area from 20 m2 g–1 for 1DL to 501 m2 g–1 for ZIF-8/1DL, together with the coexistence of micropores and newly generated mesopores. Electrochemical evaluation in lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries indicates enhanced Li-ion transport in the composite compared with 1DL alone. These findings highlight the utility of 1DL as a structural framework for MOF-based nanocomposites and provide a pathway to hierarchical designs for energy-storage applications.

title: Hierarchical Ion-Conducting Materials Based on Polymer-Aligned Nanoparticles within Poly(vinyl benzyl methoxy poly(ethylene oxide) ether)- block -polystyrene Diblock Copolymer
abstract: Abstract Solid polymer electrolytes based on poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) are promising alternatives to liquid electrolytes for safer lithium-ion batteries. Here, we report hierarchical solid polymer electrolytes obtained by selectively incorporating lithium sulfonamide-functionalized polymer nanoparticles (LiNPs) into a microphase-separated poly(vinyl benzyl methoxy poly(ethylene oxide) ether)-block-polystyrene block copolymer. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) demonstrate that the phase-segregated lamellar morphology of the block copolymer is preserved upon nanoparticle incorporation. Notably, the LiNPs preferentially localize within the poly(ethylene glycol)-rich lamellae, generating hierarchical structures with ordering across multiple length scales arising from block copolymer self-assembly, selective nanoparticle organization, and poly(ethylene glycol) crystallization. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) reveals that the crystallinity of the poly(ethylene glycol) phase depends strongly on nanoparticle loading and plasticizer content. These hierarchical electrolytes exhibit high ionic conductivity, which is further enhanced by the addition of sulfolane as a plasticizer. These results elucidate the interplay between hierarchical morphology, phase crystallinity, and ion transport in block copolymer-based solid electrolytes, providing design guidelines for mechanically robust solid electrolytes with enhanced transport performance.

title: Constructing Dinuclear Cd2-Porphyrin Motifs in Metal–Organic Frameworks to Accelerate Intersystem Crossing for Boosting Photocatalytic Aerobic Oxidation
abstract: Abstract Dinuclear metalloporphyrin cores remain elusive in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), despite their potential to direct spin–orbit coupling and triplet sensitization for efficient singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. Herein, we report a structurally precise series of Cd-porphyrin MOFs to elucidate how porphyrin-core nuclearity and coordination geometry influence 1O2 photosensitization. Solvothermal regulation affords three crystalline porous frameworks featuring a free-base porphyrin core (QPF-8), a mononuclear Cd-porphyrin unit (QPF-9), and a dinuclear Cd2-porphyrin motif (QPF-10). QPF-8 serves as an additional free-base reference, whereas the closely related QPF-9 and QPF-10 provide a direct platform for probing how mono- and dinuclear porphyrin coordination environments influence photophysical properties. QPF-10 exhibits a measured 1O2 quantum yield of 0.68, compared with 0.50 for QPF-9. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations associate the dinuclear motif with enhanced metal-porphyrin orbital mixing and a 4.59-fold increase in the calculated S1–T1 spin–orbit coupling matrix element (from 3.14 to 14.40 cm–1), supporting more effective triplet photosensitization. Consistent with these photophysical properties, QPF-10 demonstrates superior catalytic activity in the aerobic photooxidation of 1,5-dihydroxynaphthalene. Notably, its activity is approximately twice that of the archetypal PCN-224(Zn) and also exceeds that of the Pt-based QPF-1(Pt). These results identify dinuclear porphyrin coordination as a structural strategy for enhancing triplet photosensitization in crystalline heterogeneous catalysts.

title: Hidden Truchet Architecture in Zinc p -Hydroxybenzoate
abstract: Abstract We redetermine the structure of the disordered metal–organic framework Zn(hba) (hba2– = the dianion of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid). Using single-crystal X-ray diffraction measurements, we characterize the structured diffuse scattering that is experimentally observed for this material and which is characteristic of strongly correlated disorder. We use geometric and crystal-chemical arguments to propose a general model for correlated disorder in Zn(hba), and then relate this model to a specific realization of so-called Truchet tilings. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we proceed to show that the model so developed is simultaneously consistent with both the average crystal structure solution described previously and the structured diffuse scattering reported here. The existence of ordered analogues with different but related chemistry suggests scope for control over correlated disorder in this family of metal–organic frameworks. Our study illustrates the potential for a Truchet-tile formalism to help describe and understand more generally the correlated disorder that can occur in network structures.

title: From Dark Photocatalysis to Photobattery‐Type Operation: A Re‐Functionalized Ti‐MOF for Solar Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient harvesting, storage, and on‐demand release of solar energy are essential for overcoming the intermittency of sunlight and enabling continuous solar energy‐driven processes, yet achieving storage of photogenerated charge remains challenging. Here, we report a Ti‐based bipyridine MOF, COK47‐bpy, and its ReCl(CO) 3 ‐functionalized analogue, ReCl47‐bpy , as photochargeable materials for time‐decoupled solar energy utilization. Re incorporation introduces localized photosensitizing and “electron sink” sites while preserving the parent framework structure, enabling visible‐light response, faster charge accumulation, and improved charge retention. In colloidal suspension, ReCl47‐bpy reaches an electron storage capacity of 19.5 C g −1 MOF under simulated solar irradiation and retains about 70% of the stored charge after 2.5 months. The stored electrons can be released on demand for dark hydrogen (H 2 ) evolution with electron‐to‐H 2 efficiencies exceeding 90%. Beyond colloids, when fabricated as robust FTO‐supported layers, ReCl47‐bpy |FTO photoelectrodes deliver capacities of up to ∼7.0 mAh g −1 MOF upon photocharging under 1 Sun irradiation. Overall, this work establishes Re‐functionalized Ti‐MOFs as versatile platforms for solar‐driven charge storage, dark photocatalysis, and MOF‐based photoelectrodes, toward the development of next‐generation MOF‐based energy devices.

title: Photocatalytic Tandem Reaction for Urea Synthesis From Atmospheric CO 2 and N 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic urea synthesis directly from atmospheric CO 2 and N 2 offers a sustainable route to bypass the energy‐intensive Bosch–Meiser process, yet simultaneously achieving CO 2 capture and reduction, N 2 activation, and C─N coupling within a single system remains challenging. Herein, we report a two‐step tandem platform combining ionic‐liquid‐modified metal–organic framework (IL@PCN‐250‐Fe 2 Co) with a trinuclear copper‐based covalent organic framework (HTP‐Cu 3 ‐imi‐COF) for urea photosynthesis from air. The IL@MOF captures atmospheric CO 2 and photoreduces it to CO, while HTP‐Cu 3 ‐imi‐COF couples the generated CO with ambient N 2 into urea. This synergistic tandem configuration delivers a urea production rate of 259.87 µg·g cat −1 ·h −1 under air, marking the first demonstration of photocatalytic urea synthesis from atmospheric CO 2 and N 2 . In situ spectroscopic measurements and DFT calculations reveal that the imidazole‐functionalized HTP segments act as hole‐rich oxidation domains, promoting water oxidation to generate *OH species that oxidize locally enriched N 2 to *NO intermediates. Simultaneously, the Cu 3 clusters serve as electron‐rich centers for CO adsorption and activation, forming *CO that couples with *NO via the critical *OCNO intermediate toward urea formation. This work not only showcases the first photocatalytic urea synthesis from air but also establishes a modular paradigm for cascade catalysts that integrate capture and conversion toward sustainable chemical transformations.

title: Fluorinated Arylethynyl Substituents in Zn(II) Complexes of Azadipyrromethene Guide Self-Assembly in Crystals
abstract: Abstract Zn(II) complexes of 2,8-arylethynyl 1,3,7,9-tetraphenyl azadipyrromethenes are promising molecular semiconductors with strong visible-NIR absorption and a nonplanar distorted tetrahedral geometry around the Zn(II) center, but their charge transport properties are limited by the orientation and strength of intermolecular π–π stacking interactions. To optimize their intermolecular π–π stacking interactions, we explored substitution of the pyrrolic phenylethynyl groups in Zn(L1)2 at the phenyl meta positions with either fluorines (Zn(L1-m-2F)2) or trifluoromethyls (Zn(L1-m-2CF3)2). Fluorination had minimal effects on optical properties and slightly deepened frontier orbital energy levels. On the other hand, fluorination strongly affected the complexes’ molecular packing: while Zn(L1-m-2F)2 had the same C2/c space group as Zn(L1)2, the −CF3 groups in Zn(L1-m-2CF3)2 promoted a higher ordered space group of Fddd. Further, in Zn(L1)2 and Zn(L1-m-2F)2, the phenylethynyl groups stack with the core phenyls of neighboring molecules, whereas in Zn(L1-m-2CF3)2, the bis(trifluoromethyl)-substituted phenylethynyl groups of neighboring molecules stack with each other with a shorter π–π stacking distance than in the other two molecules. Computations revealed that fluorination decreases the internal reorganization energy for electron transfer and increases overlap integrals for charge transfer. Fluorination is thus a promising strategy to tune molecular packing and parameters relevant to charge transport.

title: Entropy-driven graded molecular selectivity in stacking-fault-programmed crystalline metallacycle membranes
abstract: Membrane-based molecular separations are fundamentally constrained by the lack of precisely defined transport pathways, limiting high-flux fractionation of species with subtle size differences. Here, we report a class of stacking-fault-programmed crystalline coordination metallacycle (CCM) membranes featuring programmable nanoarchitectures constructed via interfacial coordination self-assembly. By rationally tuning the angular geometry of metallacyclic precursors, we fabricate two structurally distinct membranes (CCM-1 and CCM-2) possessing ordered microporous frameworks with well-defined transport channels. Both membranes exhibit simultaneously high solvent permeance and sharp molecular sieving, surpassing the conventional permeability-selectivity trade-off. Molecular simulations coupled with thermodynamic analysis reveal that the high selectivity arises from an entropy-dominated transport mechanism, governed by stacking-fault-induced misalignment of metallacycles. This misaligned stacking generates graded steric confinement, enabling precise discrimination between molecules with minimal size differences. Furthermore, we construct a cascade separation system integrating CCM-1 and CCM-2, achieving stepwise fractionation of complex ternary mixtures, including high-value pharmaceutical compounds. The CCM membrane process demonstrates significantly lower costs, carbon emissions, and energy consumption (89% reduction) compared to traditional chromatography and distillation methods. This work establishes stacking-fault programming as a powerful design principle for crystalline membranes, providing a general strategy to engineer entropy-governed transport pathways for energy-efficient and precision separations in chemical and pharmaceutical processes. Membrane based separations can be constrained by the transport pathways in a system. Here the authors design a programmed crystalline coordination metallacycle which self-assembles to form well-defined transport channels.

title: Healthcare Waste-Derived Pyrolytic Char as a Functional Porous Carbon Material for Electrochemical Sensing of Estriol
abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated approach for the sustainable management of healthcare waste (HCW) through slow pyrolysis and the application of the resulting pyrolytic char (Pc) for electrochemical sensing of estriol (E3), an emerging contaminant, in environmental and pharmaceutical samples. Pc was produced by the pyrolysis of HCW at 400 °C and characterized by Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). Pc exhibited a mesoporous structure with a specific surface area of 6.9 m² g⁻¹, a pore volume of 0.026 cm³ g⁻¹, and an average pore diameter of 14.44 nm. Morphological analysis revealed a heterogeneous surface with a composition dominated by carbon (61.3%), oxygen (23.6%), silicon (9.6%), and aluminum (5.5%). A new conductive ink formulation was developed by modifying a commercial carbon-based ink with HCW-derived Pc, aiming to fabricate advanced and portable screen-printed electrodes for electrochemical E3 sensing. Pc proportions ranging from 1% to 10% were investigated. The sensor exhibited a high sensitivity of 58.5 nA L µmol⁻¹ and achieved a detection limit of 47.1 nmol L⁻¹ over a linear concentration range from 1.0 to 216.0 µmol L⁻¹. Recovery assays were performed in tap water, lagoon water, and pharmaceutical cream samples, yielding recoveries between 97.7% and 105.4% without the need for any sample pretreatment. These findings demonstrate that HCW-derived Pc is a promising, efficient, and sustainable sensing material for steroidal hormones, providing an integrated approach to waste valorization and environmental protection.

title: Mechanistic Insights into the Colloidal Synthesis of Monodisperse CoF2 Nanorods
abstract: Abstract Transition metal fluorides (TMFs) are promising conversion-type cathode materials for high-energy lithium–metal batteries owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, making them attractive for demanding applications such as electric aviation. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish conversion kinetics, pronounced voltage hysteresis, and poor electrochemical reversibility. Understanding the structural and chemical evolution of TMFs and the electrode–electrolyte interphase formed during cycling is essential for improving their performance. Monodisperse nanocrystalline TMFs are ideal model systems for high-resolution transmission electron microscopy because their uniform size, morphology, and electron transparency enable representative nanoscale characterization. Here, we investigate a reproducible colloidal synthesis of monodisperse, single-crystalline CoF2 nanorods and elucidate the mechanisms governing their formation to achieve precise control over particle size and aspect ratio. By independently varying reaction time, temperature, precursor composition, and ligand chemistry, we identify the key factors controlling precursor decomposition, burst nucleation, phase selection, and anisotropic crystal growth. These insights provide a transferable framework for the controlled synthesis of a broad range of transition metal fluoride nanocrystals.

title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
abstract: Abstract Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid–liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
abstract: Abstract Conventional cement-based materials face a fundamental trade-off between low density and high performance, owing to their limited ability to precisely control pore structure. We use ultrasound carbonation to tailor the water distribution and confinement within the flocculation structure, thereby directing product nucleation and growth, and ultimately yielding a multifunctional submicron-scale water-foamed cementitious material. The matrix exhibits a highly refined pore network, 96.8% of which is smaller than 200 nm. The specific compressive strength is 22.5 kN·m·kg −1 , representing an increase of up to 162% relative to a laboratory-prepared foamed concrete control. Simultaneously, the sound transmission loss increases by 131.8% and 107.0% at 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz, respectively, while cumulative CO 2 uptake reaches 7.11% per unit mass of cement after 28 days. The approach relies solely on cement and water as raw materials, reducing process complexity and showing potential for production.

title: Dual-End Interfacial Regulation via Phase-Transitioned BSA-Assisted Layer-by-Layer Assembly of Metal–Phenolic Networks for Antifouling and Antibacterial Coatings
abstract: Abstract Biofilm formation poses a persistent health risk, yet conventional antibacterial coatings offer limited resistance to the initial conditioning-film stage that precedes bacterial colonization. Herein, we report a phase-transitioned BSA (PTB)-assisted layer-by-layer strategy that constructs a sequence-controlled metal–phenolic network (MPN) coating with dual-end interfacial regulation. A bottom PTB layer serves as a versatile adhesive primer, anchoring the MPN core to chemically inert LDPE via hydrophobic and coordination interactions at the interface, while a top PTB capping layer suppresses nonspecific protein adsorption and early stage biofouling. Stepwise coating growth was confirmed spectroscopically and microscopically, with thickness and Cu-associated signal intensity increasing progressively with cycle number. Capping the MPN coating with a PTB layer markedly reduced protein adsorption and bacterial adhesion. Antibacterial activity scaled with MPN layer number, reaching near-complete eradication of E. coli and S. aureus for the 3-layer configuration. The PTB-primed architecture withstood acid, alkali, ethanol, and sonication treatments that readily delaminated the counterpart lacking the bottom PTB layer, demonstrating pronounced interfacial robustness. Moreover, the strategy translated seamlessly to glass and porous fabric without loss of structural and functional fidelity. These findings establish PTB as a versatile interfacial building block that bridges adhesion and antifouling, offering a substrate-independent platform for contamination-resistant coatings.

title: Cell-free reconstitution reveals synergistic stabilization of microtubule doublets by PACRG and FAP20
abstract: Abstract Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Cryo-tomography of in vitro reconstructed microtubule doublets in presence of PACRG and FAP20 reveals reduced B-tubule curvature fluctuations, promoting a more rigid and aligned conformation. Altogether, our findings suggest that PACRG and FAP20 function synergistically to reinforce microtubule doublet stability, ensuring ciliary integrity and function.

title: Isoreticular Contraction of kgd‐Topology Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Pharmaceutical Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide a structurally programmable platform for membrane‐based separation of small‐molecule active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). Nevertheless, constructing membrane pores with subnanometer precision and resolving structurally similar molecular mixtures remain major challenges. Herein, we report an isoreticular contraction strategy to construct a series of kgd‐topology COF membranes with progressively narrowed apertures in situ on polyacrylonitrile (PAN) substrates through contra‐diffusion interfacial polymerization between hexa(4‐formylphenyl)benzene (HFPB) and three triamine monomers of decreasing size. Systematic framework contraction decreased the aperture from 12.1 to 10.2 Å and then to 6.5 Å, giving molecular weight cut‐offs of 500, 380, and 290 Da, respectively. Notably, membranes with different contraction degrees were further integrated into a cascade separation system with well‐separated molecular‐weight rejection thresholds, enabling the purification of a four‐component mixture of camptothecin‐related compounds with equal mass concentrations, achieving a maximum fraction purity of 96.6%. This work establishes isoreticular contraction as an effective strategy for programming transport‐relevant pores in COF membranes and highlights the potential of kgd‐topology COF membranes for cascade pharmaceutical purification.

title: Securing the Future: Porous Materials in Sensors for National Defense
abstract: Abstract Engineered porous materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) offer highly tunable, unique characteristics useful for durable, low power, selective gas sensors. This Perspective describes how MOF-based porous materials fit into the quickly emerging gas sensor landscape for national defense applications, and how they are anticipated to play an increasingly important role in the future to ensure national security. Herein is described in detail the relationships between the ability to judicious select porous materials to adsorb targeted key gases and the unique electrical responses for high consequence sensing related applications. Included are the materials strengths and limitations, followed by future materials needs and application growth areas. Finally, the emerging uses of AI/ML for materials and response design are highlighted. Altogether, porous materials such as MOFs offer outstanding chemical selectivity that can be leveraged for enhanced sensing in defense applications, providing better understanding of not only materials aging, but also chemical biological, radiological and nuclear threats.

title: THE ASSEMBLY OF CHARGED LINEAR AND BOTTLEBRUSH POLYMERS AT THE INTERFACES
abstract: Assembly at the liquid-liquid interface is the spontaneous organization of molecules or particles at the boundaries between two immiscible liquids. This process is driven by the minimization of free energy and can easily be seen in biological processes like membrane formation and viral assembly.1–5 By utilizing pair-interaction, such as electrostatic interaction, and self-assembly of functional polymers, liquid-liquid interfacial assembly opens new platforms for nanotechnology and material synthesis for optical, electronic, and magnetic applications.6–8 Previous investigations within our group have explored interfaces for electronic and ion transport in all-fluid systems primarily using nanoparticles to stabilize the interfacial interaction.9–18 In this work, we presented an extended investigation into how polymer conformation and architecture (linear polyelectrolytes, bottlebrush polyelectrolytes, and linear copolymers) impact interfacial assembly in the absence of nanoparticles at both water-water and water-oil interfaces. We introduced a physically crosslinked gel matrix into polyelectrolyte complexes consisting of poly(2-(dimethylamino) ethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA), poly (sodium 4-styrenesulfonate)) (PSS) and alginate. When printed at all-aqueous interface, this hybrid system significantly enhanced mechanical integrity and selective ion transport membrane. To address the inherent instability of weak polyelectrolytes compared with strong polyelectrolyte complexes like PSS and PDADMAC (poly (diallyldimethylammonium chloride), we investigated bottlebrush polyanions with linear polycations. These new architectural combinations increased electrostatic interactions to achieve superior salt resistance and robust interfacial stability exceeding 48 hours, facilitating ion transport and drug delivery. Moving from homopolymer to copolymer, we also established a predictive relationship between bulk conformation and interfacial thermodynamics using solvent-sensitive copolymers. We demonstrated that flexible Gaussian chains in chloroform formed stable viscoelastic network at water-oil interfaces, whereas star-micelles in toluene favor desorption and interfacial instability. By correlating solubility parameters and block architecture with interfacial behavior, this work provided a framework for designing robust, all-fluid functional materials based on bulk polymer characteristics.

title: Thickness‐Gradient Liquid Metal Connectors for Seamless Electrophysiological Sensors
abstract: High-fidelity electrophysiological monitoring requires wearable bioelectronic devices with mechanical properties closely matched to human skin. However, current approaches focus primarily on electrode design and performance, while overlooking mechanical compliance and interfacial continuity with complex and dynamic human skin. Mechanical mismatches across electrodes, connectors, and interconnects often lead to interfacial noise, motion artifacts, and electrical instability. In order to overcome these critical issues, we introduce a thickness-gradient liquid metal (LM)/SEBS connector that enables seamless interfacial integration with skin, electrode, and interconnector interfaces through gradual mechanical compliance matching and manually activated metal network formation. The activated LM forms continuous and robust conductive networks, maintaining electrical stability under large tensile strain (∼1100%) and for repeatable deformation cycles. Skin-mimetic conformal integration suggested here suppresses interfacial void formation and stress concentration and thereby preserves stable electrical pathways under dynamic skin deformation. As a result, the proposed system delivers markedly improved signal amplitude and signal-to-noise ratio, along with substantially lower noise, relative to conventional connector platforms. By systematically aligning mechanical compliance across sensor components, this mechanically adaptive design preserves seamless electrical pathways and minimizes motion-induced artifacts under dynamic conditions, providing a robust platform for reliable electrophysiological monitoring in long-lasting wearable bioelectronics.

title: Electrochemical strategies for peptide synthesis, deprotection and scalable reactor technologies
abstract: Peptides have high target specificity, favourable safety profiles, and increasing applications in oncology, metabolic disorders, infectious diseases, and precision medicine, making them one of the fastest-growing classes of therapeutic molecules. Traditional peptide synthesis involves more hazardous solvents and stoichiometric quantities of coupling reagents, which lead to high process mass intensity and environmental impact. In electrochemical synthesis, electrons are traceless redox reagents that allow for the controlled activation and transformation of peptide substrates under mild conditions. Advances in electrochemical peptide bond formation, electrochemical deprotection methods, and new technologies of electrochemical reactors for peptide synthesis are critically discussed. The focus is on phosphine-mediated anodic peptide coupling, iodide-mediated amide formation, residue-selective electrochemical modifications and redox-triggered deprotection methods. Advances in flow electrochemistry, scalable reactor designs and sustainable peptide production methods are thoroughly discussed. The effect of electrochemical parameters such as the electrode materials, current density, solvent systems, electrolytes, reaction time, and reactor design on reaction efficiency and selectivity is critically evaluated. However, there are still some issues that need to be addressed, such as the scope of the substrates, the lack of understanding of the mechanisms, fouling of the electrodes, scalability and the absence of a standardized method of reporting. Opportunities for the future include the combination of electro­chemistry and continuous-flow processing, sustainable solvent systems, automated synthesis platforms, and machine learning-assisted process optimization. Electrochemical approaches provide valuable potential for development of greener, more efficient and potentially scalable technology for next-generation pharmaceutical manufacturing of peptides.

title: Protein Self-Assembly as a Design Principle for Enzyme Immobilisation in Biocatalysis
abstract: Enzyme immobilisation is essential for translating biocatalytic processes from the laboratory to industrial applications by improving enzyme stability, recovery, and reuse. It underpins sustainable processes in pharmaceuticals, biofuels, and food production, but conventional immobilisation strategies involve inherent trade-offs. Covalent attachment prevents enzyme leaching but may distort the active site, whereas physical adsorption better preserves enzyme conformation but allows enzyme leaching. Furthermore, carrier-based methods frequently encounter mass-transfer limitations and may require external cross-linkers, hindering broader industrial application. Recent advances in synthetic biology and materials science have accelerated the development of protein-based materials for biocatalysis. This review examines protein self-assembly as a unifying design principle for enzyme immobilisation, enabling programmable assembly under relatively mild conditions to overcome key limitations of conventional strategies. We discuss naturally derived structures such as bacterial microcompartments and engineered systems including virus-like particles, elastin-like polypeptides, and SpyTag/SpyCatcher, which support programmable enzyme organisation and enable compartmentalised multi-enzyme cascade reactions. Building on this, a major focus is placed on catalytically active inclusion bodies (CatIBs). As robust, intrinsically self-immobilised protein aggregates, CatIBs represent a simplified, carrier-free platform offering potential process and cost advantages for industrial biocatalysis.

title: Recent Advances in 1,8-Naphthalimide-Based Supramolecular Gels (2020–2026)
abstract: Naphthalimide (NI) derivatives constitute attractive building blocks for the construction of fluorescent supramolecular gels owing to their structural versatility, remarkable photophysical properties, and ability to participate in non-covalent interactions. These properties prompted us to write this review, that provides a focused overview of the representative advances reported between 2020 and 2026 in NI-based supramolecular gels, covering the evolution from low-molecular-weight organogelators and metallogels to peptide-based and water-compatible hydrogels. Particular attention is paid to the influence of molecular design on self-assembly and gelation, including the contribution of hydrogen bonding, π–π stacking, metal coordination, and other intermolecular interactions to the formation of fibrillar supramolecular networks. The close relationship between aggregation and the photophysical response of the NI chromophore is also discussed, highlighting phenomena such as aggregation-induced and aggregation-enhanced emission and gelation-induced fluorescence enhancement. These properties have enabled the development of stimuli-responsive materials displaying fluorescence modulation and gel–sol or gel–gel transitions, particularly in response to metal ions and chemical stimuli. Recent studies also further demonstrate a transition toward more complex functional systems, including fluorescent peptide hydrogels and thixotropic materials with potential biomedical applications. The main applications developed during this period, ranging from chemical sensing to smart fluorescent materials, bioimaging, and biomedical systems, are critically analyzed. Finally, current limitations and future opportunities for NI-based gels are discussed, with particular emphasis on the development of red and near-infrared emissive systems and advanced soft photonic materials.

title: Cold Plasma Induced 3D Printing of Hydrogels
abstract: Control over when and where gelation occurs is central to the fabrication of structured soft materials, yet most approaches rely on chemical additives or uniform bulk triggers. Here, we show that cold plasma provides an external, reagent-free route to spatial and temporal control over gelation in low molecular weight hydrogel systems. Plasma exposure induces a localised decrease in pH at the plasma–liquid interface, triggering self-assembly and gel formation only in the treated region. This external plasma-induced self-assembly method enables direct writing of gel features from precursor solutions without embedded triggers, construction of three-dimensional architectures, and control over local mechanical properties through plasma dose. Our approach also allows simultaneous formation of metal nanoparticles within gels, yielding spatially confined composite and catalytic soft materials.

title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
abstract: Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. Here, we report a bioinspired supramolecular thermistor that achieves thermal transduction through molecularly gated charge transport. The hybrid polyurethane/carboxymethyl cellulose (PU/CMC)/MXene/NiO composite integrates dynamic hydrogen-bond reconfiguration, hydrated ionic conduction, and temperature-dependent electronic transport. Upon cooling, cooperative supramolecular evolution continuously modulates coupled ionic and electronic pathways, producing an ultrahigh negative temperature coefficient of −22,280% °C −1 between −80° and −75°C. The thermistor resolves detectable temperature changes below 0.01°C while maintaining negligible hysteresis, excellent reproducibility, and effective thermal-mechanical decoupling. Combined with a dedicated low-noise readout circuit, it enables reliable monitoring of subtle temperature evolution during simulated atmospheric cooling. Integrated into a multichannel sensor array, it further provides force-independent thermal mapping for robotic manipulation. This work establishes molecularly gated supramolecular thermal transduction as a strategy for ultrahigh-resolution cryogenic temperature sensing.

title: Dynamic pore-network evolution in mesoporous CMK3@S cathodes governing sulfur conversion and electrochemical accessibility
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous carbon architectures provide high surface accessibility and interconnected transport pathways for sulfur-based energy-storage materials. However, the initial pore structure may evolve during electrochemical operation due to solid-product formation, affecting ionic transport and sulfur utilization. In this study, the dynamic structure–transport–performance relationships governing sulfur conversion in mesoporous CMK3@S cathodes for potassium–sulfur batteries are investigated using a coupled porous-electrode model. The model framework describes the coupled evolution of K⁺ transport, polysulfide redistribution, sulfur-conversion kinetics, K₂S precipitation, connected porosity, tortuosity, interfacial accessibility, and spatial reaction redistribution. The model predictions were quantitatively evaluated against reported electrochemical characteristics and independently measured transport-related properties, showing deviations within an acceptable range for electrode-scale simulations. The validated framework predicts a nonlinear transition from distributed K₂S accommodation to connectivity-sensitive pore-network obstruction during discharge. According to the simulations, moderate precipitation can be accommodated by the mesoporous framework with limited transport penalty, whereas deposition near critical transport pathways results in accelerated loss of ionic accessibility. At the simulated advanced-discharge condition, the predicted mean precipitation-blocking index (PBI) reaches 0.69, accompanied by a transport-limitation index (TLI) of 0.74, a reaction uniformity index (RUI) of 0.49, an active-depth utilization (ADU) of 58.7%, and an accessible-capacity loss (ACL) of 28.7%. Sensitivity and uncertainty analyses based on the model further identify precipitation kinetics, initial pore accessibility, tortuosity, and ionic diffusivity as key parameters controlling structural–electrochemical evolution. These results suggest that maintaining connected transport pathways during solid-product formation is critical for improving the electrochemical accessibility of mesoporous sulfur cathodes and provide a mechanistic modeling perspective for the design of precipitation-tolerant carbon–sulfur electrode architectures.

title: Stress‐Resistant Plant Cell‐Wall Inspired Cell Armor Enables Red Blood Cell Lyophilization
abstract: ABSTRACT Lyophilization offers an attractive route for ambient‐temperature storage of biological systems by eliminating cold‐chain dependence and suppressing solution‐phase degradation. However, lyophilizing mammalian cells remains challenging due to their vulnerability to coupled stresses, including ice‐induced mechanical injury and membrane destabilization during freezing and dehydration. In nature, stress‐resistant plant cells survive extreme conditions through multifunctional cell walls. Inspired by their natural survival strategies, we engineer an artificial membrane armor (AMA) that enables efficient lyophilization of red blood cells (RBCs). This biomimetic AMA integrates a nanoporous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF‐8) for mechanical support, a water‐retentive polymer matrix for hydration retention and colloidal stabilization, and Zn 2 + coordination preserves membrane fluidity and suppresses freeze‐ and dehydration‐driven membrane phase transitions. Through synergistic interfacial protection, the AMA effectively buffers coupled stresses associated with lyophilization, enabling ∼95% post‐rehydration recovery of RBCs using an ultra‐low protectant content (<5 wt%) together with an ambient shelf‐life of at least 3 months, unachievable with previous methods. Furthermore, the rehydrated RBCs preserve their native morphology, membrane mechanics, metabolic activity, oxygen transport capability, and in vivo circulation behavior. This work establishes a bioinspired interfacial engineering strategy for transferring desiccation tolerance from plants to mammalian cells, advancing ambient‐temperature biostorage of sensitive living systems.

title: Engineering pH-Responsive Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Encapsulating Demethylzeylasteral for Targeting PI3K/AKT Signaling in Pancreatic Cancer
abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for innovative strategies that improve intracellular drug delivery and target critical survival pathways. The present study investigated a pH-responsive mesoporous silica nanoparticle (MSN) system for encapsulation and delivery of demethylzeylasteral (DMZ), with particular emphasis on modulation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. DMZ-loaded pH-responsive MSNs were prepared and characterized for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, morphology, surface area, pore characteristics, drug-loading efficiency, and structural properties. In vitro release studies were performed under physiological and acidic conditions to evaluate pH-responsive drug release. The biological activity of free DMZ, DMZ-loaded MSNs, and pH-responsive DMZ-MSNs was evaluated in pancreatic cancer cells by assessing cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution, migration, and invasion. Molecular analysis was performed to determine changes in PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling and apoptosis-associated proteins. The optimized pH-responsive DMZ-MSN formulation demonstrated nanoscale characteristics, efficient DMZ encapsulation, and enhanced drug release under acidic conditions. Compared with free DMZ and non-responsive DMZ-loaded MSNs, the pH-responsive formulation exhibited enhanced cellular uptake, greater cytotoxicity, increased apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest, and stronger inhibition of migration and invasion. These effects were associated with suppression of phosphorylated PI3K, AKT, and mTOR together with increased Bax and cleaved caspase-3 and reduced Bcl-2 expression. In vivo evaluation further indicated enhanced tumor suppression with an acceptable preliminary safety profile. Collectively, the findings support pH-responsive DMZ-MSNs as a promising nanotherapeutic platform for pancreatic cancer targeting PI3K/AKT-associated survival signaling.

title: Beyond Static Crystal Cartography (GNoME) in Hydrogen Storage: Exothermic Adsorption Phonon-Gating, VASP-PyCCE (CCE-3) Defect-Tolerant "Dynamic Fingerprints," and Closed-Loop Real-Time Optimization (RTO P2.0)
abstract: While graph neural network material discovery platforms such as Google DeepMind's GNoME (Graph Networks for Materials Exploration) have cataloged over 2.2 million stable crystalline structures, these zero-Kelvin equilibrium predictions constitute "static maps" that fail to capture the non-equilibrium thermodynamic and quantum-mechanical dynamics governing real-world energy storage. When hydrogen molecules (H2) rapidly infiltrate mesoporous Metal-Organic Frameworks (specifically Cu(PC)/C60@MIL-101(Al)-d4), the exothermic heat of adsorption (Delta H_ads) excites localized lattice vibrations (structural breathing modes), inducing thermal jitter (T_jitter >= 0.5 ms), spin decoherence, and transport bottlenecks. This monograph unifies four foundational pillars into a complete mathematical and experimental protocol: (1) Dynamic Hydrogen Storage & Exothermic Phonon-Gating: Redefining the spin-diffusion barrier perimeter (Zone II, 4.0 A <= r <= 6.6 A, anchored by critical site Index 45 at r = 5.03 A, A_zz = 3.006 MHz) as an Adaptive Phonon-Gate that nonlinearly upconverts Delta H_ads via d4-BDC linker torsional modes into delocalized acoustic phonons, recovering eta >= 21.74% of thermal energy to lower H2 diffusion barriers ("turning thermal noise into a transport accelerator") while preserving room-temperature spin coherence (T2 = 9.8 ms); (2) Bridging the Screen-to-Lab Gap: Coupling first-principles VASP (PAW+HSE06) electric field gradient (EFG) and hyperfine tensors with Cluster-Correlation Expansion (PyCCE / CCE-3) spin-bath generators that natively ingest stochastic wet-synthesis vacancies, linker disorientations, and trace solvent noise to output low-dimensional, non-destructive Dynamic Fingerprints {L(t), S(omega)}; (3) Closed-Loop Lab-to-Fab Actuation: Real-Time Optimization (RTO P2.0) audited over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (F_p, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) via QFS-zkVM and Human-in-Command (HIC) interlocks; and (4) Strategic Synthesis: A keynote paradigm shift from static material screening to dynamic physical-layer energy storage. title: Composition-Optimized Mesoporous SrTiO3/rGO Composite Electrodes for High-Performance Asymmetric Supercapacitors
abstract: Abstract Composite electrodes substantially enhance supercapacitor performance through the synergistic effect of their constituent materials. In this study, strontium titanate (STO) nanoparticles were anchored onto and within the layers of reduced graphene oxide (rGO) to develop high-performance STO/rGO composite electrodes. A series of composites with varying weight ratios was synthesized to determine the optimal configuration for supercapacitor applications. Brunauer−Emmett−Teller (BET) analysis, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) were used to thoroughly analyze surface, morphological, and structural features. A three-electrode configuration was utilised to evaluate electrochemical performance parameters. In a 1 M NaOH electrolyte, the STO/rGO (1:2) composite demonstrated the maximum specific capacitance of 1133 F g−1 at 5 mV s−1. It also demonstrated outstanding cycling stability, holding onto 73.3% of its initial capacitance after 10,000 galvanostatic charge−discharge (GCD) cycles. STO/rGO (1:1) also demonstrated the maximum specific capacitance of 270 F g−1 at a current density of 9 A g−1. To demonstrate practical applicability, an asymmetric prismatic lab-scale supercapacitor device (STO/rGO || NaOH || ACb) was fabricated, and three devices connected in series successfully powered three LEDs (red, yellow, and green). These results highlight the strong potential of STO/rGO composites for advanced energy-storage technologies.

title: Accessing Diverse C(sp3)-Rich Cyclophane Linkers in Macrocyclic Peptides via Nickel-Mediated Deaminative Macrocyclic Arylation
abstract: Abstract Within macrocyclic peptides of both natural products and pharmaceutical targets, aryl rings play a crucial role in linker structure, and C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers can imbue beneficial physicochemical properties. Yet, methods to deliver C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers remain limited, restricting the types of carbon-rich linkers that can be efficiently investigated in medicinal chemistry campaigns. Herein, we describe the development of a nickel-mediated deaminative macrocyclic arylation that uses amino acid monomers compatible with solid-phase peptide synthesis workflows, accommodates a wide range of peptide functionalities, and can access broad macrocycle architectures including those of a natural alkaloid derivative and polycyclic peptides.

title: A Histidine-Mediated, Pendulum-Like Proton Transport Mechanism Is Required for the High Catalytic Activity of [FeFe]-Hydrogenases
abstract: Abstract [FeFe]-hydrogenases are molecular hydrogen (H2) converting enzymes that employ a hexanuclear iron complex, the H-cluster, as the catalytic cofactor, and a proton transfer pathway (PTP) that enables efficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Recent phylogenetic analyses have revealed different groups of [FeFe]-hydrogenases. Although only very few members of other groups have been characterized, current knowledge suggests that high catalytic activity is predominantly associated with group A members. Here, we show that metal ions inhibit group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases by binding to three specific residues at the entrance of the PTP. Exchanging residue H565 of Clostridium pasteurianum CpI results in a metal-insensitive protein variant with wild-type-like activity. In contrast, exchanging S320 and H569 in CpI, and their counterparts in additional group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases results in enzymes with markedly decreased activities and large overpotential requirements. These features are consistent with important roles of both residues in catalytic proton transfer. CpI structures reveal that H569, locally anchored by E278, can be present in two conformations, such that we propose a histidine-dependent pendulum mechanism for exchanging protons between the bulk solvent and the PTP, which is well supported by theoretical calculations. In doing so, our study broadens understanding of how histidine mobility, governed by neighboring residues in the vicinity, contributes to the fundamental concept of PCET.

title: Aliphatic Diazonium Chemistry through Hydroquinone-Based Nitrate Reduction for Deaminative Halogenation and Nitrate Ester Formation
abstract: Abstract Alcohols are readily converted to electrophiles on a large scale, while deaminative functionalization of aliphatic amines is less developed. Aromatic amines are readily used as versatile synthetic intermediates through diazonium chemistry, but analogous aliphatic diazonium chemistry is currently not as useful because of the instability and explosiveness of aliphatic diazonium intermediates. Here, we develop aliphatic diazonium chemistry through nitrate reduction-based diazotization with substoichiometric hydroquinone as a chemically competent reductant. As a consequence, the deamination allows Sandmeyer-type reactivity to convert aliphatic amines into alkyl (pseudo)halides. Because all of the reagents are inexpensive, aliphatic diazonium chemistry provides potential access to alkyl halides and alkyl nitrate esters on scale.

title: Bromide–Borate Coupling Enables Selective Electrochemical Oxidation of Glycerol to Dihydroxyacetone
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective electrochemical valorization of biodiesel‐derived glycerol is challenged by competing oxidation pathways that generate complex product mixtures. Here, we report a bromide–borate‐mediated indirect glycerol electrooxidation for selective dihydroxyacetone (DHA) production on carbon electrodes. Bromide is electrochemically converted into soluble oxidized bromine species that mediate homogeneous glycerol oxidation, whereas borate provides a weakly alkaline bromine‐speciation window and coordinates glycerol to bias C3‐product formation toward DHA. At identical pH, borate favored DHA formation, whereas phosphate shifted selectivity toward glyceric acid. Under optimized conditions using 100 mM glycerol and 100 mM KBr in 1 M borate buffer solution (pH 8.2), divided H‐cell electrolysis afforded DHA with 75% relative selectivity and high overall Faradaic efficiency (FE). Recirculating flow‐cell operation increased DHA selectivity to 80% while maintaining high overall FE, and one‐way flow‐cell achieved a DHA production rate of 1205 mmol m −2 h −1 .

title: Bimetallic Coinage Metal Complexes of Tetradentate ortho ‐Ter‐arylene Ligands
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a series of photoluminescent bimetallic Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I) complexes supported by tetradentate donor‐acceptor ligands containing two monoanionic amide donors (D) and two aza‐arene acceptors (A). The metal complexes of the ligand containing carbazolide and pyridyl ligating groups possess high photoluminescence quantum yields (up to 65% in solution) and emission properties consistent with thermally‐activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Bimetallic Cu(I) complexes of similar ligands containing benzannulated donor (benzo[a]carbazolide) or acceptor (isoquinoline) moieties demonstrate that absorption/emission properties are tunable by modification of D/A groups. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction of the bimetallic complexes reveals metal–metal distances shorter than the sum of their van der Waals radii, suggesting metallophilic interactions between the d 10 metal centers. Ultrafast excited‐state kinetic analysis reveals nearly equal exergonic intersystem crossing rates between Cu(I) and Au(I) complexes, contrary to what is expected from each metal's spin–orbit coupling contributions. These findings are corroborated with theoretical modeling, which suggests that the optical transitions of these bimetallic complexes are characterized as metal–ligand‐to‐ligand charge transfer (MLLCT) states.

title: Smart Piezoelectric Hybrid Ceramic Membrane With the Capacity of Pulsed Responsive Self‐Cleaning and Anti‐Fouling Functions
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic fouling remains a major challenge for ceramic membrane filtration because of the strong adsorption of organic foulants on membrane surfaces. Herein, a novel design strategy is proposed for smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes featuring self‐powered nano‐brushes. Specifically, a self‐powered nano‐brush smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membrane (ATPAA − ‐PBM) with the pulsed pressure responsiveness and self‐cleaning capability was prepared by grafting negatively charged sodium PAA polymer chain (PAA − ) on the surface of BaTiO 3 (BTO) piezoelectric ceramic membrane. Under the pulsed pressure, alternating piezoelectric charges induced reversible conformational oscillations of the self‐powered nano‐brushes, promoting the detachment of the foulant layer by the flowing water and thereby enabling in situ self‐cleaning. Meanwhile, the grafted PAA − nano‐brushes strongly associated with water molecules to establish a 462 nm‐thick hydration layer, while generating electrostatic repulsion toward humic acid (HA), jointly preventing foulant adhesion and enabling nearly complete rejection. The membrane exhibited outstanding retention, anti‐fouling ability, and remarkable flux retention ratio (FRR = 92.3%, 10 d) during a long‐term filtration process. Consequently, a novel excellent rejection and anti‐fouling mechanism of “self‐powered nano‐brush dynamic oscillation self‐cleaning & hydration barrier” was proposed. This study provides a new perspective for the fabrication of self‐cleaning smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes.
